issues.legal_issue: A person who purchases land after publication of a preliminary acquisition notification cannot use that purchase to claim valid title against the acquiring State.
material_facts: A preliminary notification had been published before the appellant purchased the land under a registered sale deed.
The appellant later constructed a house on the land.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s post-notification purchase could not give him valid title against the State; upon acquisition and possession, the land would vest in the State free from encumbrances.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16 of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953, after possession is taken the land vests in the State absolutely, free from encumbrances. A purchase made after the Section 4(1) notification cannot be asserted against the State to obtain title. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity or effect of a land acquisition.
predicates.purchase_after_initial_notification: The claimant acquired the land after the preliminary acquisition notification had been published.
predicates.post_notification_purchaser_cannot_asser: A purchaser who acquired the land after the preliminary notification cannot assert valid title to it against the acquiring State.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition is challenged and the claimant acquired the land after the preliminary notification, the claimant cannot assert title against the State.

issues.legal_issue: An interval between a preliminary acquisition notification and a later declaration does not invalidate the acquisition where the interval is explained by preparation and approval of the acquisition scheme, and a later purchaser cannot rely on that interval to challenge the acquisition.
material_facts: The preliminary notification preceded the declaration by a substantial period.
After the preliminary notification, an improvement scheme was prepared and sent to the government for finalisation and approval.
The appellant purchased the land after the preliminary notification.
issues.conclusion: The delay did not invalidate the acquisition: the time taken for the scheme’s preparation and approval did not amount to inordinate delay, and the appellant, having purchased after the preliminary notification, could not rely on the interval to challenge it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered Sections 4(1) and 6 of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953. It held that time taken to prepare and obtain approval for the improvement scheme did not make the valid preliminary notification invalid, and that a purchaser who acquired land after that notification could not rely on the interval between notification and declaration. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity or effect of a land acquisition.
predicates.purchase_after_initial_notification: The claimant acquired the land after the preliminary acquisition notification had been published.
predicates.scheme_preparation_and_approval_accounte: The period before the later declaration was used to prepare and obtain approval for the acquisition scheme.
predicates.interval_does_not_invalidate_acquisition: The interval between the preliminary notification and the later declaration does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition challenge, a post-notification purchase or an interval accounted for by scheme preparation and approval means that the interval does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: An exemption wrongly granted to another landholder does not entitle a claimant to the same exemption under the principle of equality.
material_facts: An adjacent nursery had received an exemption from acquisition.
The appellant’s residential site was not exempted, and he sought the same benefit.
issues.conclusion: The exemption granted to the adjacent nursery did not entitle the appellant to an exemption, and the claim of discrimination under Article 14 failed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 of the Constitution does not require an authority to extend a benefit granted through wrongful action to another person; a wrongful exemption does not create a right to equal treatment in that wrong. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity or effect of a land acquisition.
predicates.claimant_seeks_same_exemption: The claimant seeks an exemption because another landholder received one.
predicates.comparator_exemption_was_wrongful: The exemption received by the other landholder was granted through wrongful action by the authorities.
predicates.wrongful_exemption_does_not_require_equa: A wrongful exemption granted to another person does not require the same exemption to be granted to the claimant.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition challenge, a claimant who seeks the same benefit as a person whose exemption was wrongful is not entitled to that benefit merely on grounds of equality.

issues.legal_issue: A later notice referring to a subdivision of a survey number does not invalidate an acquisition notification that identified the parent survey number.
material_facts: The preliminary notification identified the main survey number.
A later notice referred to a subdivision of that survey number.
issues.conclusion: The difference between the main survey number in the preliminary notification and the subdivision number in the later notice did not invalidate the acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(1) of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953, identification of the main survey number in the preliminary notification is sufficient; details of its subdivision may be supplied at the appropriate stage. A later reference to a subdivision does not vitiate the notification. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity or effect of a land acquisition.
predicates.parent_survey_number_identified_initiall: The preliminary acquisition notification identified the parent survey number for the land.
predicates.subdivision_identified_in_later_notice: A later notice identified a subdivision of the survey number identified in the preliminary notification.
predicates.survey_number_difference_does_not_invali: The difference between the parent survey number and its later-identified subdivision does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition challenge, when the initial notification identifies the parent survey number and a later notice identifies its subdivision, that difference does not invalidate the acquisition.
